raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36651

## Summary

- **cumem.py**: Track per-allocation mapped state to prevent double `cuMemRelease` when `sleep`/`wake_up` are called on already-unmapped or already-mapped allocations. Add a `sleeping` flag so `_python_free_callback` returns a dummy handle during sleep, avoiding CUDA ops on freed memory. Remove `gc.collect` + `empty_cache` in `sleep()` which can trigger frees during the sleeping window.
- **cumem_allocator.cpp**: Clear stale `error_code` at the top of `create_and_map`, `unmap_and_release`, and `my_free` to prevent leftover errors from previous operations propagating. Skip CUDA ops in `my_free` when `recv_d_mem == 0` (sleeping block already freed). Fix size mismatch by using `recv_size` instead of `size` in `unmap_and_release` and `cuMemAddressFree` calls. Log a warning when `unmap_and_release` fails and `cuMemAddressFree` is skipped to make virtual address leaks visible.
- **rotary_embedding/common.py**: Replace `find_spec` check with `try/except` for `flash_attn.ops` import to support Flash Attention 4 which restructured its module layout.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `sleep()` / `wake_up()` cycles work without CUDA errors in colocated training
- [ ] Verify no regressions in standard vLLM inference with cumem allocator enabled
- [ ] Verify rotary embedding works with both Flash Attention 2/3 and Flash Attention 4

Hi @markrogersjr — we ([intarweb](https://github.com/intarweb)) are tracking this fix because we hit it in production (mxbai-rerank-large-v2, 412 MiB → 5184 MiB residual GPU growth over ~24h of sleep/wake cycles; cross-confirmed in vllm-project/vllm#36651 [earlier today](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36651#issuecomment-4663559852)).

I rebased your two commits onto current `main` (mergify flagged conflicts on 2026-05-23). Pushed to https://github.com/intarweb/vllm/tree/rebase/cumem-pr36535 (tip `ee20a10764defae12b7069d7a3639e3849de7ea6`).

**Rebase resolutions** (two non-trivial conflicts, both mechanical):

1. **`vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py`** — upstream refactored `HandleType` and `AllocationData` out of this file into `vllm/device_allocator/__init__.py`. Dropped your inline duplicate definitions and moved the new `mapped: bool = True` field onto the canonical dataclass in `__init__.py`. `xpumem.py` also uses `AllocationData` and is unaffected (default `True`). Also dropped the unused `import gc` per your cleanup commit's intent (the cumem.py hunk already auto-merged the commented-out `gc.collect()`/`empty_cache()` removal).

2. **`vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/common.py`** — upstream added a `not current_platform.is_cpu()` guard before the `flash_attn` import. Preserved that guard around your `try`/`except` so CPU builds still skip the import. Final shape:

   ```python
   self.apply_rotary_emb_flash_attn = None
   if not current_platform.is_cpu():
       try:
           from flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary import apply_rotary
           self.apply_rotary_emb_flash_attn = apply_rotary
       except (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError):
           pass
   ```

3. `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` auto-merged cleanly.

**Sanity check** (no GPU/CUDA on my laptop, can't do a full build): all 3 modified Python files parse via `ast.parse`; no conflict markers; brace depth unchanged in the C++ file. Per-commit attribution preserved (your authorship + Signed-off-by); commits signed.

Happy to open a fresh PR superseding this one if maintainers prefer, or you can pull from `intarweb:rebase/cumem-pr36535` directly — whichever helps land it sooner. We're planning to deploy a build off this branch on our GPU host this week regardless, so we'll have residual-memory data to share if useful.

## Code Review

This pull request addresses several critical issues in the `cumem` allocator, particularly around the `sleep`/`wake_up` functionality. The changes prevent double-free errors by tracking allocation mapping state and handle stale error codes by resetting a global error variable. The use of a `sleeping` flag to manage frees during the sleep window is a good solution. Additionally, the update to support Flash Attention 4 by using a more robust import mechanism is a welcome improvement. Overall, the changes are well-reasoned and correctly implemented. I have one point of feedback regarding error handling in `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp`, where the current fix for preventing crashes could lead to a silent resource leak. Addressing this would make the error handling more robust.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This error handling logic, while preventing a crash from calling `cuMemAddressFree` on a still-mapped memory region, introduces a silent virtual address space leak. If `unmap_and_release` fails, `cuMemAddressFree` is skipped, but the address space reserved by `cuMemAddressReserve` for `d_mem` is never freed. In long-running applications, this can lead to resource exhaustion. Consider logging this event as a warning to make debugging easier if memory issues arise later.

         # these ephemeral bound-method objects being garbage collected.
         # See discussions in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/22724
@@ -164,6 +165,9 @@ def _python_free_callback(self, ptr: int) -> HandleType:
         """
         Internal method to look up the allocation data
         when memory is freed in the memory pool."""
+        if self.sleeping:
+            self.pointer_to_data.pop(ptr, None)
+            return (0, 0, 0, 0)
         data = self.pointer_to_data.pop(ptr)
         if data.cpu_backup_tensor is not None:
             data.cpu_backup_tensor = None
@@ -197,6 +201,8 @@ def sleep(self, offload_tags: tuple[str, ...] | str | None = None) -> None:
         backup_bytes = 0
 
         for ptr, data in self.pointer_to_data.items():
+            if not data.mapped:
+                continue

@@ -212,6 +218,7 @@ def sleep(self, offload_tags: tuple[str, ...] | str | None = None) -> None:

         )
 
-        gc.collect()

+        self.sleeping = True
 
     def wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> None:

@@ -237,8 +243,10 @@ def wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> None:

         for ptr, data in self.pointer_to_data.items():
             if tags is None or data.tag in tags:
-                handle = data.handle
-                create_and_map(handle)

@@ -248,6 +256,7 @@ def wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
                         cpu_ptr = cpu_backup_tensor.data_ptr()
